name: eval-entity-name-match

messages.content:
Teaching examples below use fictional Example-prefixed entities; they are not factual claims.

Are these two names referring to the SAME real-world organization/company, or are they DIFFERENT organizations that merely share some words?

Judge SAME when:
- They differ only by abbreviation, truncation, punctuation, or spelling (e.g. "TK" / "Techniker Krankenkasse", "eVisit NB" / "eVisitNB").
- One name is the bare brand/company name and the other is that SAME brand name plus a generic descriptor tacked on (industry type, "Health", "Partners", "Group", "Associates", "EHR", "Center", etc.) -- e.g. "Spire" / "Spire Orthopedic Partners", "Allianz" / "Allianz Partners", "NextGen" / "NextGen EHR". The brand word itself is the identity; a generic suffix doesn't change the company.

Judge DIFFERENT when:
- The names only share a GENERIC word (an industry term like "Health", "Specialists", "Orthopedics") with no shared brand/distinctive word -- e.g. "ExamplePayments" / "Baptist Health", "UW Health" / "Duke Health".
- One name has an extra SPECIFIC qualifier the other lacks -- a place name, person's name, or other distinguishing detail that isn't generic -- e.g. "UC Health" / "UC San Diego Health" (San Diego is specific, not generic), a bare word appearing unrelated inside another org's parenthetical.

Name A: {{name_a}}
Name B: {{name_b}}

Answer with exactly one word: "same" or "different".
